messages:
pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT alert: trigger kv-cache.eviction_rate > 80% for service=runtime/predict in prod us-east-1. Multiple 95th/99th latency breaches. Paging oncall: @maya. Link: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/kv-cache

maya: I'm oncall, jumping in. Looking at grafana now — 95th for /predict at ~1.8s -> spikes to 6-8s. KV entries increased ~4x in last 10m.

maya: Running quick checks: kvcache size by shard shows shard-3 growth; eviction rate high, lots of long-running batches aligned with the spike.

raj: I'm seeing batch-scheduler queueing long requests. Mixed short/long workload causing pack-shed starvation. There are many big batches waiting because window_ms grew. Correlates with a config rollout at 10:12.

max: yep I rolled a batch config earlier today to increase batching_window_ms to 120 and max_batch_size to 256 for throughput tests. I didn't expect KV hotset blowup. Rolling back now.

max: rolling revert command: ```
curl -X POST https://infra-api.redwood/configs/batch-scheduler/apply \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"max_batch_size":64,"batching_window_ms":20}'
```

ops-bot: Deployment log: config-revert-batch-1958765450 started by max. CI checks passed.

elin: Manual ops: starting targeted kv-eviction on shard-3 to shed the hotset while revert propagates. Running:
```bash
redis-cli -h kv-shard-3 --scan --pattern "user:*:embedding" | xargs -n 100 redis-cli -h kv-shard-3 del
```
Note: doing in small batches to avoid thundering herd.

maya: Good. After revert we should see batch latencies drop in 1-2 min. Watching tail now.

luis: Support notes: we've had 5 customer reports from prod (IDs: C-824, C-831, C-842, C-845, C-849) complaining about predictions timing out or >5s latency. Two are on dedicated instances. I've opened customer tickets and set initial severity to S2; notifying account teams.

raj: Observed metrics update: once revert took effect at 1958765512, number of large batches dropped ~78% and queue wait time fell. But KV cache still highly resident — eviction backlog causing sustained tail.

maya: action: keep manual eviction running, throttle incoming long requests if possible. Can we temporarily disable continuous-batching for endpoints with long model runs?

max: we can flip a per-route flag. Patch deploying now to set batching_policy=prefer-prefetch for /predict-long so they don't pack with short requests. Command: ```
POST /runtime/routes/update {"route":"/predict-long","batching_policy":"separate"}
```

ops-bot: Patch deployed by max at 1958765678.

elin: After evictions and the revert, most shards show lower memory pressure. I'm seeing eviction_rate normalize on shard-3. Still doing a gradual TTL trim job to return to baseline.

maya: Customer impact summary (so far): 5 customer tickets, estimated 1-2% of total requests saw >2s extra latency during the 17m window. No errors returned, mainly latency spikes and a couple truncated streams.

caroline: From product: assign a postmortem and a set of actions: 1) rollback guard on batch config changes for prod (block increase >2x without canary), 2) route-level batching separation by default for long-running models, 3) add KV-residency alert and auto-evict policy threshold, 4) update runbook to include manual eviction steps.

maya: I'll own the runbook update and immediate follow-ups. max to own the config guard, elin to own auto-evict policy proposal, raj to own scheduler fairness work. caroline will shepherd the postmortem.

sre-lead: Escalation accepted. Please add time ranges, graphs, and exact config diff to the incident doc. We'll review in ops review tomorrow. Thx all.

maya: Handoff: I'm keeping this open for the next 45m then handing to raj for long-term mitigation work. Current status: revert complete, manual evictions ongoing, per-route batching patched, customer comms in flight.

luis: Noting customers notified, follow-up emails queued with root-cause summary once we have postmortem.

ops-bot: Incident update: severity downgraded to S3 at 1958766000. Runbook link: https://wiki.redwood/incidents/1958765432

maya: Closing notes for thread: need retrospective on deploy gating and canarying for batch-scheduler params. Also evaluate KV guardrails so config tweaks can't cause cache blowups. I'll create the postmortem ticket and ping owners.

caroline: Thanks everyone — good coordinated response. We'll take the action items into the sprint. :thumbsup:
